nodes.label: package.json
nodes.summary: Defines the Football Life Next.js application package, including development, build, start, lint, and Prisma seed scripts plus the core runtime stack: Next.js 15, React 19, Prisma 7 with PostgreSQL adapter, Supabase SSR/client libraries, TanStack Query, Framer Motion, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, Zod, and Upstash rate limiting.
nodes.name: package.json

nodes.label: Core Game Logic Systems Map
nodes.summary: System-wide audit of the Football Life career loop. It maps setup, yearly wheel progression, season simulation, growth, transfer, continental qualification, persistence, and retirement as one causal graph where OVR, club context, competition outcomes, match rating, growth, and squad rating feed each other. It records correctness and balance risks, rejects per-spin server round trips at scale, and proposes a three-tier architecture of pure shared logic, client orchestration, and authenticated server checkpoints.
nodes.name: core-game-logic-systems-map.md

nodes.label: Core Transfer Design
nodes.summary: Transfer market design source for soft contracts, market value, transfer fees, wages, renewals, shortlist approaches, and free-agent unemployment. It locks the use of euro-thousand integer units, K=3 inbound offers, club buying-power bands derived from prestige and league tier, mandatory buyout affordability filtering, career-length contract clamping, approach acceptance odds, and the rule that player flexibility may affect wage/signaling but never reduce the current club buyout.
nodes.name: core-transfer-design.md

nodes.label: Core UI/UX Design SoT
nodes.summary: UI/UX overhaul source of truth for presentation-only improvements. It locks the wheel as the visual and interaction backbone, preserves the existing careerSubStep flow and cream/pitch/gold/Panini visual language, rejects logic or formula changes in the UI pass, and defines handcrafted layout rules such as a season strip, story rail, wheel hero, Panini side card, stakes-specific skins, transfer decision theatre, motion guidance, token hygiene, acceptance criteria, and phased delivery.
nodes.name: core-ui-ux-design.md

nodes.label: Transfer Window Preview Page
nodes.summary: Development-only client page that renders a mocked TransferMarketResult through TransferWindowPanel. It exercises renewal, inbound transfer offers, shortlist approach odds, affordability blocking, willing-to-move state, shortlist visibility, and action logging without calling server actions.
nodes.name: page.tsx

nodes.label: Transfer Window Panel
nodes.summary: Client presentation component for the transfer window. It displays current contract state, market value, mandatory buyout, renewal offers, inbound offers capped at three, shortlist approach cards with accept percentages, rejected approach badges, an Available toggle that explicitly does not reduce buyout, and the special unemployment CTA for free-agent windows.
nodes.name: TransferWindowPanel.tsx

nodes.label: Competition Labels
nodes.summary: Pure TypeScript lookup module for domestic cup names, league confederations, and continental cup display labels. It keeps leagueId-based cup names aligned with the league seed data, provides a deprecated league-name fallback matcher, and maps continental cup codes such as UCL, Libertadores, AFC_CL, CONCACAF_CC, and CAF_CL to user-facing labels.
nodes.name: competitions.ts

nodes.label: Transfer Economy Helpers
nodes.summary: Pure transfer economy library implementing the locked transfer design numbers. It derives club buying-power bands from prestige and league tier, clamps contract years to remaining career and a hard cap, computes market value from OVR, age, form, and remaining contract, derives mandatory buyout, checks affordability, proposes wages and contract years, decides renewal eligibility, formats euro-thousand values for UI, estimates expected apps, and computes shortlist approach acceptance chances without randomness.
nodes.name: transfer-economy.ts

nodes.label: Supabase Auth Middleware
nodes.summary: Next.js middleware that creates a Supabase SSR server client, refreshes authentication with auth.getUser, redirects unauthenticated users to /login, redirects authenticated users away from /login to the lobby, and permits development-only /dev routes while excluding static assets from the matcher.
nodes.name: middleware.ts

nodes.label: Club Seed Data
nodes.summary: Static CLUBS seed dataset for the 2025/26 football world included by the app. Each club record carries id, name, leagueId, prestige, historical league/domestic/continental title counts, and current continentalType so career setup, transfer filtering, competition qualification, prestige thresholds, and continental cup syncing can use consistent club metadata.
nodes.name: clubs.ts

nodes.label: League Seed Data
nodes.summary: Static LEAGUES seed dataset listing supported tier-one and tier-two competitions by id, display name, country, tier, prestige, domesticCupName, and confederation. The data anchors club league relations, domestic cup labeling, confederation lookups, and transfer buying-power tier inputs.

nodes.label: Prisma Schema

It defines GameSession ownership and squad state, CareerPlayer identity, career arc, stats, hidden server-only stats, season history, transfer economy fields, unemployment flag, and club stints/events JSON, plus League, NationalTeam, and Club models used by seed data, career setup, competitions, and transfer systems.

edges.summary: The systems audit points transfer design to core-transfer-design.md for market browse, contracts, fee, wage, buying power, and the transfer checkpoint model.
The transfer document positions transfer as a core career subsystem and cites the systems map for checkpoint timing and scale constraints.
The UI SoT uses the systems map as the technical source for the locked season pipeline and explicitly forbids UI work from changing that logic.
The UI SoT delegates transfer economy rules to the transfer design document and scopes transfer UI work to presentation of the already locked logic.
The development preview page imports and renders TransferWindowPanel with mocked transfer market payload and local UI state.
The middleware exempts /dev routes outside production, allowing this preview page to be opened during development without the normal auth redirect.
TransferWindowPanel uses transfer-economy formatting and approach-percent helpers to display fees, wages, market value, buyout, and shortlist acceptance odds.
Transfer economy calculations align with CareerPlayer transfer fields such as contractYearsTotal, contractYearsRemaining, currentWageAnnual, marketValue, and isUnemployed.
The league seed objects populate the League model fields id, name, country, tier, prestige, domesticCupName, and confederation.
The club seed objects populate the Club model fields id, name, leagueId, prestige, title counts, and continentalType.
Every club seed uses a leagueId that refers to one of the league seed ids, forming the Club-to-League relationship used by Prisma and game logic.
Competition cup and confederation lookups are keyed by league ids and documented as being kept in sync with the league seed data.
Competition labels complement club continentalType values by turning domestic league ids and continental cup codes into gameplay display names.
Buying-power bands depend on league tier values supplied by league records and propagated through transfer market candidates.
Buying-power, affordability, expected apps, and approach odds depend on club prestige and league tier metadata carried by seeded clubs.
The panel presents market value, wage, contract years, buyout, and unemployment concepts that are persisted or derived from CareerPlayer transfer fields.
